c1_lamp.title: A lamp above a blue door
c1_lamp.note: "Do you still light the lamp above the blue door?" The recipient promised to keep a lamp burning until the writer came home.

c1_cinnamon.title: Cinnamon at four in the morning
c1_cinnamon.note: "The whole street smelled of it at four in the morning." Something cinnamon, made every day before dawn — such as dawn is, here.

c1_funeral.title: Papa's funeral
c1_funeral.note: The writer said something cruel at their father's funeral, twelve years ago. "Papa" — so they shared a father with the recipient?

c1_ferry.title: The 8:15 for Hushwater
c1_ferry.note: The writer is somewhere the 8:15 ferry to Hushwater leaves from — and keeps not getting on it.

c1_hotel.title: Harbor Arms letterhead
c1_hotel.note: Written on cheap hotel paper from Port Ardent, the city across the bay. Recently, by the look of the ink.

c1_dark_lamp.title: Mari's dark lamp
c1_dark_lamp.note: Above the bakery's blue door hangs an iron lamp, cold and dark. Its wick has been trimmed down to nothing.

c1_po_lamp.title: Odile's burning lamp
c1_po_lamp.note: The post office has a blue door too — and Odile's lamp burns above it, as it has every night for fifty years.

c1_tea.title: Odile's cinnamon tea
c1_tea.note: A cold cup on the counter. Odile drinks cinnamon tea by the potful.

c1_cinnamon_sign.title: Cinnamon loaves at four
c1_cinnamon_sign.note: The bakery's chalkboard: CINNAMON LOAVES AT 4 O'CLOCK, EVERY MORNING. The whole square must smell of it.

c1_theo.title: Mari's brother Theo
c1_theo.note: Mari's younger brother Theo left Hushwater on the night ferry after their father's funeral, twelve years ago. No one has heard from him since.

c1_dockman.title: The man on the far dock
c1_dockman.note: Every night, a big man on the Port Ardent dock buys a ticket for the 8:15 and never boards. Bram says he has Mari's eyes.

c1_only_child.title: Odile was an only child
c1_only_child.note: Odile had no brothers or sisters. Her father went to sea when she was four and never came home. There was no funeral.

c2_dear_t.title: Addressed to "T."
c2_dear_t.note: Someone whose name begins with T.

c2_lamp.title: "If you light the lamp tonight"
c2_lamp.note: The writer asked the lighthouse for an answer. The recipient was the one who would light it.

c2_married.title: To be married on Sunday
c2_married.note: The recipient was about to be married, in October 1985.

c2_pier.title: The end of the pier
c2_pier.note: "If the lighthouse stays dark, I'll be waiting at the end of the pier."

c2_date.title: 13th October, 1985
c2_date.note: Forty-one years ago — the night before a wedding.

c2_violet.title: Violet ink
c2_violet.note: The letter is written in violet ink, gone brown at the edges. An unusual choice.

c2_inkwell.title: Odile's violet inkwell
c2_inkwell.note: Odile writes everything in violet ink — bread orders, lighthouse bills, labels. She always has.

c2_rosa.title: Tobias and Rosa
c2_rosa.note: Tobias Fenn married Rosa on a Sunday in October 1985. Rosa died twenty years ago.

c2_photo.title: An old photograph
c2_photo.note: On Tobias's windowsill: two young people on the pier in the summer of '85. She wears round spectacles. He is looking at her, not the camera.

c3_stargazer.title: "Dear Stargazer"
c3_stargazer.note: Both letters are addressed to someone who watches the stars.

c3_ferry.title: "We got on the ferry"
c3_ferry.note: The recipient is thinking of leaving Hushwater on the ferry — for good.

c3_grandpa.title: Grandpa's lamp
c3_grandpa.note: The recipient's grandfather keeps a lamp that matters enough to go dark. The lighthouse?

c3_rosa_stars.title: Stars named for Grandma
c3_rosa_stars.note: The recipient's grandfather named stars for his wife — and never told anyone.

c3_postmark.title: Postmarked 2046
c3_postmark.note: SOUTHERN OCEAN · 14 MAR 2046. Twenty years from now.

c3_comet.title: A grumpy comet
c3_comet.note: The stamp shows a small, cross-looking comet. "I've named a comet."

c3_manifest.title: The ferry manifest
c3_manifest.note: Bram's manifest: J. FENN — ONE WAY — 15 OCT — 6:10. The morning after Lantern Night.

c3_june_scope.title: June's telescope
c3_june_scope.note: June spends every night at the end of the pier with a brass telescope her grandfather gave her.

c3_felix_scope.title: Felix's telescope
c3_felix_scope.note: A telescope pokes out of the clock tower balcony. Felix sets his clocks by the stars, and calls himself "a student of the heavens".

c3_star_chart.title: Rosa's Crown
c3_star_chart.note: In the lamp room, a star chart: three small stars circled in pencil, labelled ROSA'S CROWN · 14.X.85.

c3_granddaughter.title: Tobias's granddaughter
c3_granddaughter.note: June Fenn is Tobias's granddaughter. Her father Daniel was his son.

c34_same_hand.title: The same hand, twice
c34_same_hand.note: Both Stargazer letters are in the same handwriting, written on the same day, 14 March 2046 — from two lives that can't both happen.

c4_keeper.title: "I'm the keeper now"
c4_keeper.note: In this future, the writer keeps the lighthouse, as her grandfather did.

c4_stairs.title: A hundred and twelve stairs
c4_stairs.note: The writer climbs 112 stairs to the lamp every night.

c4_112.title: 112 steps to the lamp
c4_112.note: Painted over the lighthouse door: 112 STEPS TO THE LAMP.

c4_sunrise.title: "I've never seen a sunrise"
c4_sunrise.note: The writer has never seen the sun rise. Not a real one.

c4_june_sunrise.title: June's sunrise
c4_june_sunrise.note: June was a baby when the dusk came. She has never seen the sun rise — and it's the one thing she wants.

c4_logpaper.title: Logbook paper
c4_logpaper.note: Torn from a HUSHWATER LIGHT logbook. Written by whoever keeps the lighthouse, twenty years from now.

c4_date.title: 14 March 2046
c4_date.note: Twenty years from now — the very same day as the airmail letter.

c4_birthday.title: June's birthday
c4_birthday.note: June was born on the 14th of March. Both letters were written on her thirty-seventh birthday.

c5_umbrella.title: The green umbrella
c5_umbrella.note: The recipient carries a green umbrella, even when it isn't raining.

c5_thursday.title: Thursdays on the 6:10
c5_thursday.note: The recipient rides the 6:10 ferry every single Thursday.

c5_crusts.title: Crusts that smell like heaven
c5_crusts.note: She feeds the gulls the crusts of something wonderful. Bread?

c5_wheel.title: "The man at the wheel"
c5_wheel.note: The writer steers the ferry — and has for thirty-one years.

c5_ticketbook.title: Ticket-book paper
c5_ticketbook.note: Written on a blank Morning Lark passenger ticket. Someone who works the ferry.

c5_po_umbrella.title: Odile's green umbrella
c5_po_umbrella.note: A green umbrella stands in the post office's umbrella stand — furled tight and furred with dust.

c5_bakery_umbrella.title: Mari's green umbrella
c5_bakery_umbrella.note: A green umbrella hangs by the bakery door, still beaded with sea spray. It was her mother's.

c5_flour_run.title: Mari's Thursday flour run
c5_flour_run.note: Every Thursday, Mari takes the 6:10 to Port Ardent for mill flour, and feeds the gulls her crusts on the way.

c5_never_leaves.title: Odile never leaves
c5_never_leaves.note: Odile hasn't set foot off Hushwater since the night of the Long Storm. Not once.

c5_blush.title: Bram's blush
c5_blush.note: Asked about green umbrellas, Bram went red to the ears and talked about clouds for five minutes.

c6_daniel.title: Addressed to Daniel
c6_daniel.note: The letter is for someone called Daniel — who was out at sea that night.

c6_1152.note: "It is 11:52." The very minute the town clock stopped.

c6_clockroom.title: The clock room
c6_clockroom.note: Written from inside the clock tower, during the storm.

c6_marguerite.title: The Marguerite
c6_marguerite.note: Daniel was aboard a boat called the Marguerite on the night of the Long Storm.

c6_dark.title: The dark lighthouse
c6_dark.note: "Why is the lighthouse dark?" On the night of the storm, the light went out.

c6_typed.title: A high-striking 'e'
c6_typed.note: Typewritten. Every 'e' sits a hair above the line — a worn type-bar.

c6_date.title: 14 October 2009
c6_date.note: The night of the Long Storm. Seventeen years ago.

c6_typewriter.title: Felix's typewriter
c6_typewriter.note: The old typewriter in Felix's workshop window. Its 'e' strikes high.

c6_memorial.title: The Marguerite memorial
c6_memorial.note: LOST WITH THE MARGUERITE, 14 OCT 2009 — DANIEL FENN, beloved son, husband and father.

c6_logbook.title: Tobias's logbook
c6_logbook.note: 14 Oct 2009: "Daniel by at nine. Taking Harrow's shift — Felix white as a sail. D. says don't let Felix know I know."

c6_mari_daniel.title: Mari's husband
c6_mari_daniel.note: Daniel Fenn was Mari's husband. Some mornings she still sets out two mugs.

c6_june_daniel.title: June's father
c6_june_daniel.note: June was six months old when her father was lost. She has one photograph of him, and nothing else.

c6_tobias_guilt.title: The lamp that failed
c6_tobias_guilt.note: The automatic lamp failed at 11:40 on the night of the storm. Tobias was asleep. He has lit it by hand every night since.

c6_felix_shift.title: Felix's shift
c6_felix_shift.note: Felix was meant to crew the Marguerite that night. He called in sick. Daniel Fenn took his place.

c7_bird.title: "My little bird"
c7_bird.note: A pet name. Someone in Hushwater is somebody's little bird.

c7_ticket.title: A ticket in a coat pocket
c7_ticket.note: The recipient has a ferry ticket hidden in their coat.

c7_uncle.title: The uncle who left
c7_uncle.note: The recipient's uncle left Hushwater in the night, without a word.

c7_flour.title: A bakery bag
c7_flour.note: Written on a Sleepless Loaf paper bag, flour in the creases. The writer is the baker.

c7_june_bird.title: June, the little bird
c7_june_bird.note: "Mum calls me little bird. I hate it. Don't tell her I said that." — June

c7_wren_bird.title: "Off you go, little bird"
c7_wren_bird.note: Bram called you "little bird" when you stepped off the ferry. You are, after all, named after one.

c8_1140.title: Eleven forty
c8_1140.note: On Lantern Night, the automatic lamp will fail at 11:40. Someone must be in the lamp room.
